qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: >90% client retention; insurance brokerage commissions scale with P&C premium inflation, providing high switching costs in middle-market commercial accounts.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (REJECT). Relies on continuous debt issuance to fund programmatic broker rollups, violating the peace-of-mind fortress balance sheet standard: $12.1B long-term debt ($10.7B net debt) on $1.49B net income equals 7.2 years Net Debt (>4.0y ceiling), and EBIT/Interest is 3.9x (<5.0x baseline).
qualitative.evidence: Arthur J. Gallagher is a premier middle-market commercial insurance broker with >90% client retention and strong tangible returns, but fails Gate 6 due to structural leverage and serial debt-funded M&A rollups. Net debt of $10.7B ($12.1B debt less $1.4B cash) against $1.49B TTM net income requires 7.2 years of owner earnings to retire, significantly exceeding the 4.0-year ceiling. Interest coverage of 3.9x ($2,510M EBIT / $639M interest expense) breaches the >5.0x threshold. In August 2025, AJG closed the $13.5B+ acquisition of AssuredPartners funded by heavy debt and equity issuance, pushing goodwill and intangibles to $33.3B against $23.3B equity (negative tangible book value of -$10.0B). With management signaling $12B in additional M&A capacity through 2026-2027 and continuing regular bolt-ons (5 acquisitions in Q3 2026 alone), the business permanently relies on debt capital markets to fuel growth, triggering the disqualifying serial rollup red flag under Gate 6.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
